decision_log.decision: L-1011 Length range '54.17–50.05 m' is DESCENDING (master verbatim)

normalization_decisions.rule: Aircraft model name verbatim per Wikipedia Wide-body aircraft master comparison table. 15 closed values. Naming convention: 'Manufacturer + Numeric Model Designation' (e.g., 'Boeing 747' not 'B-747' or '747'; 'Airbus A300' not 'A-300'; 'McDonnell Douglas DC-10' not 'DC-10'; 'Lockheed L-1011' not 'L-1011 TriStar' — master uses bare 'L-1011' without TriStar suffix; 'Ilyushin Il-86' / 'Ilyushin Il-96' with hyphen between Il and number). Alphabetical sort places Airbus A300-A380 first, then Boeing 747-787, then Ilyushin, Lockheed, McDonnell Douglas.

Text year-range with end-marker per master verbatim. Range format: '[start year]–[end year]' for completed production (e.g., '1974–2007' A300; '1968–2023' Boeing 747); '[start year]–present' for in-production (e.g., '1994–present' A330; '2007–present' Boeing 787). Exception: Ilyushin Il-96 uses hyphen NOT en-dash ('1992-present') — master-source verbatim variant preserved per cycle-1 audit. Mostly en-dash '–' except Il-96.

Maximum Takeoff Weight in metric tonnes per master verbatim. Mostly single-value numeric (e.g., 171.7 A300, 575 A380). Boeing 777 has range '351.5–365.7' reflecting MTOW variation across 777-300ER / 777-9 variants. Text type preserves the range when present (vs forcing numeric central).

Compound text format 'metric value(s) m (imperial value(s) ft in)' per master verbatim. Single-value: '46.66 m (153 ft 1 in)' A310; '72.72 m (238.6 ft)' A380. Ranges: '53.61–54.08 m (175 ft 11 in – 177 ft 5 in)' A300 with en-dash and possible spaces around imperial-range em-dash. L-1011 has descending range '54.17–50.05 m (177.7–164.2 ft)' reflecting variant chronology — preserved verbatim. Master uses mixed imperial precision (some 'ft in' notation like '193 ft 0 in', some decimal-feet '218.5 ft'); preserve master's variant per cell.

Text format '[count] ([status/date marker])' per master verbatim. Examples: '561 (discontinued)' A300; '1663 (March 2026)' A330 (in-production count as of master date); '34 (2025)' Il-96 (low-production count); '254 (discontinued)' A380 (final after 2021 production end). Production counts for in-production aircraft (A330 / A350 / 767 / 777 / 787) carry March 2026 or February 2026 dates reflecting recent master update; production-end aircraft carry '(discontinued)' marker.

open_questions.question: Why is Comac C929 excluded from the universe?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-1 audit BLOCKING #2: Comac C929 (the 16th row in Wikipedia Wide-body aircraft master comparison table) is projected with 2029- first-flight date AND empty Number Built value. Universe filter locks to 'has Number Built value' = built/produced; C929 fails this filter. When C929 enters service post-2029 and has documented Number Built, universe can extend 15 → 16. Mirror precedent for incumbent/projected exclusion: NATO SG / Chief Justices / British monarchs (current incumbents excluded with similar future-extension provision).

open_questions.question: Why is Il-96 Produced cell '1992-present' with hyphen instead of en-dash?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-1 audit verbatim dump: Wikipedia master Wide-body aircraft comparison table cell for Ilyushin Il-96 uses regular hyphen '-' between '1992' and 'present', while other Produced cells use en-dash '–'. This is a master-source inconsistency preserved verbatim per source-extractive principle. Curator-normalization to uniform en-dash would introduce normalization NOT in source. Documented as known master variant.

open_questions.question: Why is L-1011 Length range '54.17–50.05 m' descending?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-1 audit master dump: Lockheed L-1011 (TriStar) had variants — the original L-1011 was 54.17 m; the shortened L-1011-500 long-range variant was 50.05 m. Master appears to list the variant lengths in chronology order (standard first, then shortened variant). The cell is preserved verbatim including the descending order — unusual but source-verbatim.

open_questions.question: Why no Comac aircraft if China builds wide-bodies?
open_questions.answer: Comac C929 is China's first wide-body project, in development with target 2029 first flight; no Comac wide-body has been built yet (the Comac C919 in service is narrow-body NOT wide-body, so out of scope). When Comac C929 enters service with documented Number Built, universe extends 15→16.

open_questions.question: What's the difference between Wide-body aircraft and Twin-aisle aircraft scope?
open_questions.answer: 'Wide-body' and 'twin-aisle' are equivalent terms in aviation — both describe aircraft with 2 passenger aisles (vs single-aisle narrow-body aircraft like 737 / A320). Master article uses 'Wide-body aircraft' as the canonical term. Universe scopes to commercial passenger families (excludes military variants like KC-10/KC-46, excludes cargo-only conversions, excludes purely freighter-built variants if Wikipedia master excludes them).
